readsAs: an 'i' whose dot leaps up in a bouncing arc
a ball being thrown or a comet trail
a tadpole or sperm shape over a separate stem
judge.why: The warm plum-and-orange wordmark feels reassuring and active, but the leaping i-dot is a familiar trope with an unfortunate tadpole read, the custom t adds noise, and the cut-out symbol leaves the stem stranded and badly balanced, so it falls apart as an app icon at small sizes.

readsAs: abstract K built from three rounded capsule strokes
a leg bending at the knee, like a progressive range-of-motion sequence
judge.why: The three-stroke K suggests guided movement in a warm, friendly way, but the cramped crescent join between the diagonal and the foot leaves a fussy sliver and a sharp spur that look accidental, and at 16–24px the mark breaks into three blobs, so it needs refinement before it is shown.

readsAs: metronome with its pendulum swung to one side
a dumbbell or knob on a rod against a tilted pyramid
judge.why: The metronome-and-slider idea is executed cleanly in a warm indigo and coral, but it reads first as a music or audio tool rather than physiotherapy recovery, and the slider knob turns into an unclear blob at 16–32 px.
